The Iran deal MOU is expected to be signed Sunday in Geneva by VP Vance and Iran's Parliament Speaker Qalibaf — with Hormuz reopening language and 60-day sanctions relief included. If confirmed, HOLD upgrades to BUY at Monday's open. A new structural risk emerged: Warsh plans to eliminate the dot plot at the June 17 FOMC — removing forward guidance since 2012 and amplifying post-meeting market volatility regardless of the rate decision. Morning HOLD call was correct (base case scenario played out). Three of five regime indicators remain in breach: VIX ~18.9 (above 18), 30Y ~5.02% (above 5.00%), SPX below 7,460; Brent and DXY are both cleared. HOLD at medium conviction — BUY conditions are within reach but the Warsh dot-plot elimination introduces a structural unknown that prevents a conviction upgrade.

bear_case: The Iran-Geneva MOU represents the fourth ceasefire framework in this conflict cycle — structurally identical to the April 7, April 21, and May 29 agreements that each collapsed within 48–96 hours of announcement. Vance's Saturday travel to Europe and reported text finalization by Saturday night are encouraging, but the Ayatollah and IRGC commanders have rejected finalized agreements at the last minute three times previously; Iranian officials as recently as Friday morning stated that final positions were still being negotiated. If the Sunday signing collapses, Brent snaps to $92–95, DXY re-breaches 100, and the BEARISH verdict activates at Monday's open. Separately, the Warsh dot-plot elimination creates a uniquely dangerous FOMC scenario: markets have never priced policy from a Fed Chair who communicates without the standard projection framework, and Warsh's first unscripted press conference without a dot plot could produce policy opacity that forces a reflexive risk-off move regardless of the underlying rate stance — the 30Y could spike above 5.15% on pure forward-guidance uncertainty, even if the rate decision itself is neutral. A deal collapse combined with a hawkish Warsh press conference would be the stagflation-plus-policy-opacity scenario that sends SPX from 7,431 to 7,200 before Juneteenth. **Invalidation: If Iran deal is formally signed Sunday in Geneva with Hormuz reopening language AND Warsh delivers clear, neutral policy communication on June 17 (dot plot or not) AND 30Y remains below 5.10% post-FOMC AND SPX closes above 7,460 for two consecutive sessions — HOLD converts to BUY. If deal collapses AND Brent breaks $92 before Monday open — HOLD converts to STEP ASIDE immediately without waiting for a session close.**
